pages.text: At midday, while Aisha's mother was resting in her room, Aisha wanted to go in to get her reading book. She ran and raised her hand to push the door suddenly.

Aisha remembered her father’s words when they had memorized together the words of Allah: ﴿يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لِيَسۡتَـٔۡذِنكُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُكُمۡ وَٱلَّذِينَ لَمۡ يَبۡلُغُواْ ٱلۡحُلُمَ مِنكُمۡ ثَلَٰثَ مَرَّـٰتٖ﴾. Interpretation of the meaning: 'O believers, let those in your service and your children who have not yet reached maturity ask your permission at three times.'
Aisha stood calmly at the door, knocked three gentle and polite knocks, and said in a clear, sweet voice: 'Assalamu alaykum, may I come in, Mama?'
Her mother gave permission with a warm smile and said, 'Come in, my dear. May Allah bless you and your adab.' So Aisha entered with dignity and joy.

Her mother taught Aisha that young children ask permission before coming in at three times: before the dawn prayer, at the midday rest, and after the night prayer — and that asking permission keeps everyone at home comfortable and increases the love between them.
Aisha always sought permission before entering any room or house, and she became a role model for her sisters and friends in practicing the beautiful akhlaq of isti'dhan.
